This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Shashidaharan.K who met with road traffic accident.

2. The petition averments in brief are that : On 11-06-2024 at about 11-30 to 11.50 p.m.,
Shashidaharan.K as a pedestrian, was standing to cross B.M Road, near Empire Hotel along with his friend Jayanth, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-10-AK-2288 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the pedestrian ie., Shashidaharan.K result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

So far, the petitioners have spent more than Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc.
3.
Prior to the accident, Shashidaharan.K was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 32 years.
He was Engineer by profession and working in a Private Company drawing monthly salary of Rs.60,000/-.
Due to the sudden demise of Shashidaharan.K, the petitioners have suffered mental agony.

4. The respondent No.1/Insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-10-AK-2288 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.1 has contended that petitioners are not the legal heirs of the deceased as petitioner no.1 is the married sister and she is residing in her matrimonial house and petitioner no.2 is the elder brother residing separately hence, they are not the dependents of the deceased.

It is further contended that there is delay in lodging the complaint,
that there is no nexus between the injuries and death, that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself but not on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. Respondent no.2/ RC owner of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-10-AK-2288 has filed written statement and contended that his vehicle was insured with the respondent no.1 and the policy was in force and that the driver of Car was holding valid and effective driving license and that the alleged accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased who was carelessly and recklessly crossing the road where there is no zebra crossing.

sentences.text: The Learned counsel for respondent no.1 has seriously disputed the allegation made by the petitioners against the driver of the offending vehicle stating that the driver of the offending vehicle has contributed sole negligence.

It is vehemently submitted that the deceased had crossed the road at the place where there is no provision to cross the road and deceased had crossed the road against to the traffic rules hence only abated charge sheet was filed even against the deceased u/Sec. 177, 179 of IMV Act along with Sections under IPC.
14.

If the police records are perused, it is true that though the complaint was lodged against the driver of the offending vehicle but after investigation charge sheet was filed even against the deceased.
It is not in dispute that at the time of accident, deceased was crossing the National Highway ie., Mysore - Bengaluru road.
It is further not in dispute that at the time of accident offending vehicle was proceeding from Mysore towards Bangalore.
It is a double road of the width of nearly 40 feet.
There is a divider in between two roads.
The spot of accident is on the extreme right side of Mysore _ Bengaluru Highway.
It is true that since Mysore- Bengaluru is one way road, the vehicles are plying in the said road from Mysore towards Bangalore.

Hence, when the width of the road is sufficiently wide to an extent of 40 feet, the driver of the offending vehicle could have drive his vehicle on the left side of the side road but he took the vehicle towards extreme right side of the road touching to the divider and hit to the deceased who was standing by the side of the divider.

As observed supra, respondent no.1 has vehemently contended that the place at which deceased had crossed the road is a restricted area wherein pedestrian/publics were prohibited from crossing the road.
15. But this court is of the opinion that pedestrians are strictly prohibited from crossing the road provided there is other provision to cross the road.
It is true that crossing dangerously or in undesignated areas is considered a major safety risk and is discouraged.
Pedestrians do not have an absolute right to cross any where at any time, they have a right to safe passage.
The passengers have to use designated areas due to the high risk of fatal accidents.

Though the respondent no.1 has stated that the place at which deceased had crossed the road is a restricted area and that there is no zebra crossing, but no suggestion was posed to the PW.1 that the deceased had crossed the road where there is no zebra crossing.

Further the deceased had already crossed the road and he was standing near the divider, under such circumstances had the driver driven his vehicle with all care and caution on the left side of the road without taking the vehicle on the extreme right side of the road this accident would not have occurred.
At the same time, crossing the road dangerously in the National Highway is also to be avoided.

16. Now in order to assess the percentage of negligence contributed by the deceased and the driver of the offending vehicle, it is better to have glance on the judgment reported in ILR 1998 Kar 1934 between Sri Narasimhaiah Vs. The General Manager & Anr.,

18. In MFA NO.2380/2016 between Smt. Gangamma Vs., Sri. Vardharaju & Anr., in the said case also referring some of the judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it has observed that "where the person is crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing and accident occurs,

In the present case, considering the fact that deceased was standing near the divider and the driver of the offending vehicle took the vehicle on the extreme right side of the road and hit to the deceased who was standing on the extreme right side of the road, the negligence contributed by the deceased can be assessed at 15% and the negligence contributed by the driver of the offending vehicle is assessed at the ratio of 85%
Hence, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in Partly Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:-
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel, it is not in serious dispute that deceased was died in the road traffic accident.

The petitioners have produced Ex.P.10/Aadhaar card of the deceased which discloses that the date of birth of deceased was 30-06-1991 and as the accident in question has taken place in the year 2024, it can be said that deceased was aged about 33 years as on the date of accident.
21. As per the case of petitioners, the deceased was Engineer by profession in a Private Company drawing monthly salary of Rs.60,000/-.

In order to prove the education qualification of the deceased and his employment, the petitioners have produced Convocation issued by Mangalore University, Marks Card issued by Mysore University, Bank statement of ICICI account No.781301000083 from date of 01-01- 2024 to 06-08-2024, Bank statement of ICICI A/No. ending with 2520 from dated 01-04-2024 to 11-06- 2024, offer letter issued by Cognitron, Offer letter of People Logic, Salary slips from People Logic from September 2023 to December -2023 at Ex.P12 to Ex.P18.
If the documents are perused, the deceased is a meritorious student scored 9.383 CGPA in his Bachelor of Computer Application and has completed his Bachelor of Computer Applications with distinction.
As per the evidence of PW.3 the deceased had left the job in the year 2024 and started his own Private start up and from the said business he was earning sum of Rs.60,000/- per month.
To prove the income, petitioners have produced the bank statement.

But the said document does not disclose the exact business which the deceased was running during the time of accident but the Ex.P17 and Ex.P18 produced by the petitioners discloses that till the month of December - 2023 he was working in People Logic Business Solutions Private Limited and he was drawing monthly salary of Rs.31,534/- and after deduction of profession tax his monthly salary was Rs.31,334/-.

In order to prove the relationship of deceased with the petitioners, they have produced the Aadhar cards, which discloses that petitioner no.1 is the married sister and she is residing in her matrimonial house and petitioner no.2 is the major brother residing separately from the deceased as the address of the deceased and petitioner no.1 and 2 are entirely different.

Though the learned counsel for respondent no.1 during the course of argument has submitted that the petitioner no.1 is not the direct sister of the deceased but no single suggestion has been posed to the PW.1 denying her relationship with the deceased, instead through out the cross examination of PW.1, the deceased was referred to as the brother of the petitioner no.1.
Hence, it can be said that petitioners are the sister and brother of the deceased.

24. So far as the dispute raised by the respondent no.1 regarding the maintainability of the claim petition filed by the petitioners and questioning the dependency of the petitioners on the income of the deceased is concerned, the PW.1 has deposed that though petitioners and deceased were residing separately but since deceased was unmarried he used to financially assist them in their day to day life.

The Learned counsel for petitioners at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in 2020 ACJ 759 (SC) between National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Birender & Ors., wherein contention was raised that claim for loss of dependency due to death of mother who was a government servant is unavailable to sons who are married and gainfully employed; they may be entitled to compensation under conventional heads.

sentences.text: So far as the dependency of the petitioners on the income of the deceased is concerned, the deceased was aged about 33 years as mentioned in the Aadhar card.
As per the own evidence of PW.1, petitioners are married having their own family and are the earning members of the family.

In a judgment rendered in SLP Civil No.7805/2022 between The New India Assurance Company Ltd.
Vs., Ananda Pal & Ors., the petitioners being the brothers of victim are older married brothers residing with their respective children.
It was observed that all though occasional help could be provided by the deceased for his family members that cannot alter their status to that of dependents.

In the said case, reliance was placed on the judgment rendered in (2009) 6 SCC 121 between Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "where the deceased was a bachelor and the claimants are the parents, the deduction follows a different principle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In regard the bachelors, normally, 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses, because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to spend more on himself.
Even otherwise, there is also the possibility of his getting married in a short time, in which event the contribution to the parent(s) and siblings is likely to be cut drastically.

Further, subject to evidence to the contrary, the father is likely to have his own income and will not be considered as a dependent and the mother alone will be considered as a dependent and the mother alone will be considered as a dependent.

In the absence of evidence to the contrary, brothers and sisters will not be considered as dependents, because they will either be independent and earning, or married, or be dependent on the father".
29.

In MFA No. 103546/2019 between Raju Singh Vs. Sharanappa & Ors., decided on 11-11-2020, it was observed that the petitioners being the brothers of the victim have not placed any piece of evidence on record to demonstrate that they were dependent on the deceased younger brother.
It is also not forthcoming as to whether the younger brother was contributing to the welfare and maintenance of the claimant.
It was further observed by referring the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court that "the legal representative of the deceased have a right to apply for the compensation.

Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being the legal representatives have a right to apply for the compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

30. In AIR 2007 Supreme Court 1474 between Smt. Manjuri Bera Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd it was observed that " where a legal representative who is not dependent files application for compensation, the quantum cannot be less than the liability referable to Sec. 140 of the Act .

sentences.text: It was observed that "the law contemplates two categories of damages on the death of a person.
The first is the pecuniary loss sustained by the dependent members of his family as a result of such death.
The second is the loss caused to the estate of the deceased as a result of such death.
In the first category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, as trustees for the dependents beneficially entitled.

In the second category, the action is brought by the legal representatives, on behalf of the estate of the deceased that the compensation, when recovered, forms part of the assets of the estate".

Hence, out of Rs.31,334/-, if  is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased there remains Rs.15,667/- per month as the savings of deceased.
Since deceased was aged about 33 years the multiplier applicable is 16.

Hence, the loss of estate would be (Rs.15,667/-x 12 x16) = Rs.30,08,064/-.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.90,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Shashidaharan.K who met with road traffic accident.
On the basis of the complaint lodged by Rajashekhar, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0096/2024 of Channapatna Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.
The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279,
337, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.177, 179 of MV Act.

REASONS 10. ISSUE No.1 :- Petitioners have categorically contended that On 11-06-2024 at about 11-30 to 11.50 p.m., Shashidaharan.K (here in after called the deceased) as a pedestrian, was standing to cross B.M Road, near Empire Hotel along with his friend Jayanth, at that time the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-10- AK-2288 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the pedestrian ie., Shashidaharan.K result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is vehemently submitted that the deceased had crossed the road at the place where there is no provision to cross the road and deceased had crossed the road against to the traffic rules hence only abated charge sheet was filed even against the deceased u/Sec. 177, 179 of IMV Act along with Sections under IPC.
14.
Hence, when the width of the road is sufficiently wide to an extent of 40 feet, the driver of the offending vehicle could have drive his vehicle on the left side of the side road but he took the vehicle towards extreme right side of the road touching to the divider and hit to the deceased who was standing by the side of the divider.
Hence, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
If the police records are perused, it is true that though the complaint was lodged against the driver of the offending vehicle but after investigation charge sheet was filed even against the deceased.
15. But this court is of the opinion that pedestrians are strictly prohibited from crossing the road provided there is other provision to cross the road.
It is true that crossing dangerously or in undesignated areas is considered a major safety risk and is discouraged.
Pedestrians do not have an absolute right to cross any where at any time, they have a right to safe passage.
The passengers have to use designated areas due to the high risk of fatal accidents.
Further the deceased had already crossed the road and he was standing near the divider, under such circumstances had the driver driven his vehicle with all care and caution on the left side of the road without taking the vehicle on the extreme right side of the road this accident would not have occurred.
At the same time, crossing the road dangerously in the National Highway is also to be avoided.
17. In an un-reported judgment rendered in MFA No. 7070/2015 (MV) between Smt.Mina Limbu &

Since both deceased and respondent no.1 had contributed negligence to the extent of 15:85 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioners have to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.

41. Issue No.4 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 2 and 3 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.31,41,164/- (Rupees Thirty One Lakhs Forty One Thousand One Hundred Sixty Four only) The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay 85% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.26,69,989/- (Rupees Twenty Six Lakh Sixty Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Eighty Nine only) with interest there on at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner no1 is entitled for Rs.13,34,995/- Petitioner no 2 is entitled for Rs.13,34,994/-
Out of the compensation awarded and interest to the petitioner no.1 and 2, 50% shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50%

Draw award accordingly.
